A1.justification: The shared authors, augmented-encoder construction and Wasserstein-correlation objective establish continuity despite the changed title and extensive revision. Both PDFs, including their equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 3 and Tables 1–2 report original structure-preservation and classification experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10 and STL10. Appendix C includes additional empirical convergence observations.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original classification, structure-preservation and collision-rate measurements across multiple objectives, pretrained networks and datasets.

M1.justification: V2 retains the augmented-encoder and Wasserstein-correlation mechanism but adds Markov-Wasserstein minimization as a second principal objective. Its anchored MSE loss maps both clean and augmented features toward the corresponding frozen clean features, requiring matching input and output spaces (Section 3.3.1). This is a new training procedure, distinct from v1's optional decoder reconstruction loss.

E1.justification: V2 adds TinyImageNet with 200 classes and a selected 50-class subset, extending evaluation beyond v1's coverage. STL10 and its four augmentation types remain. CIFAR10 experiments and the quantitative MNIST classification suite disappear; MNIST remains as a dimensionality-reduction and rotation-invariance illustration.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated SimCLR and HSIC training objectives to the STL10/DINOv2 and SwAV comparisons, including classification and geometry measurements. The end-to-end classifier comparator remains, while v1's PCA comparison is removed. The additional pretrained backbones are experimental settings rather than competing adaptation methods.

E3.justification: V2 replaces the earlier multilayer encoders with 4096-unit, one-hidden-layer adapters and evaluates full-dimensional and quarter-dimensional outputs. It adds CLIP, R-DINO and supervised ResNet50 feature settings. Structure evaluation shifts from persistence, spectral and heat-kernel distances to pairwise-distance distortion, Lipschitz bounds and regression/RMSD measures; collision testing adds rigid alignment. The principal epoch and augmentation-sampling defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds raw-versus-aligned collision analysis, investigates MaWa failure on supervised ResNet50, compares full versus reduced WaCo dimensions, and examines class-count/separation effects using TinyImageNet. V1's encoder-versus-decoder ablation and numerical convergence observations for increasingly demanding composite augmentations are removed. The MNIST rotation illustration retains its earlier qualitative question.

E5.justification: Section 4.1.2 newly introduces ordinary-least-squares fitting of original versus encoded distances, reporting estimated slopes, intercepts and R2; this statistical fitting procedure is absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, so this addition does not establish improved run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 2 reports 91.30% rotated-image accuracy for the DINOv2 WaCo linear classifier; v2 Table 2 reports 91.19% at the same output dimension but with a revised architecture. V2 also adds MaWa results, including 94.66% rotation and 86.09% noise accuracy in Table 1, new comparator and TinyImageNet results, and supervised-ResNet50 failure findings. V1's PCA/topological result entries are removed.

T1.justification: V2 adds formal definitions of collision-free augmentations, collision rate and structure-constrained post-training invariance, plus the derivation of MaWa as anchored MSE. It removes v1's adapted-dependence theorem, barycenter corollary, empirical double-sum proposition and their Appendix B proofs, as well as conditional Wasserstein dependence. The retained Wasserstein-correlation and Markov-kernel background is largely relocated.

C1.justification: Post-training invariance, already an application in v1, becomes v2's central research problem. The abstract, contributions and conclusion foreground two adapter objectives, preservation of pretrained metric structure and comparisons against SimCLR/HSIC. V1's broader representation-learning/compression framing and explicit contribution claim for adapted-dependence theory are substantially revised.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes metric preservation from semantic clustering and explains why WaCo is unsuitable as a generic representation-learning objective. It introduces collision-based applicability boundaries, interprets MaWa's supervised-ResNet50 failure and WaCo's relative resilience, and acknowledges the unresolved justification for replacing ordinary correlation maximization with its sliced counterpart. The earlier limitation concerning complex augmentations remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B updates architecture specifications and adds explicit classifier dimensions, SimCLR's batch-size exception, additional backbone identifiers and A100 hardware. The advertised code repository changes from wasserstein_correlation_maximization to augmentation_invariance. Most optimizer, scheduler, epoch and augmentation defaults repeat v1 Appendix C; v1's explicit standard-split statement is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning through dedicated discussions of self-supervised learning, fine-tuning/adapters and optimal-transport applications. Newly cited adaptation work includes Kumar et al. (2022), Rebuffi et al. (2017) and Dukler et al. (2023). Its novelty positioning centers on structure-preserving post-training invariance rather than primarily contributing to transport-based dependence measures.

P1.justification: The title changes to Post-Training Augmentation Invariance, and the abstract, introduction, contribution narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work is subdivided, key background moves into the main text, methods and experiments are reorganized, and dedicated limitations and future-work subsections replace the earlier compact conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the classification and structure-preservation tables and adds an extensive standardized table appendix. Four distance-scatter figures with fitted and reference lines are introduced. The noise t-SNE comparison expands to five panels, while the retained MNIST rotation comparison becomes a two-panel Figure 6; both t-SNE figures appear at the document's end.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for its central goal: v1's PCA comparison tested ordinary compression, whereas v2 Tables 2–5 directly measure geometry preservation in invariant adapters against alternative training objectives. The simple MaWa objective, TinyImageNet evaluation and documented ResNet50 failure clarify practical usefulness and applicability boundaries. These gains outweigh the removal of v1's adapted-dependence proofs and compression benchmarks, although WaCo's theoretical guarantees and run-to-run uncertainty remain unresolved.
